subject: Pilot readiness: recommended models, perf profiles, and bench links
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot readiness: recommended models, perf profiles, and bench links

Hi Elise —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and the recommended next steps to get a pilot you can validate end-to-end. TL;DR: we recommend starting the pilot with the Redwood-13B-int8 variant as the primary candidate and Redwood-7B-quant as a cost-efficient fallback for higher TPS spikes.

Call takeaways:
- Target workload: conversation summarization + short Q&A (avg input 280 tokens, expected output 40–80 tokens).
- Desired baseline: 15 concurrent requests/sec sustained during peak windows; p50 latency target <= 120ms, p95 <= 320ms.
- SLO sensitivity: you flagged p99 tail behavior as important for UX.

Recommended configuration (initial pilot):
- Primary model: Redwood-13B-int8 (verified profile attached) — measured on G4dn-like nodes: 13B int8: 18 TPS avg; latency p50 95ms, p95 290ms, p99 540ms for 80-token responses.
- Fallback model: Redwood-7B-quant for burst scaling — 35 TPS avg; p50 60ms, p95 160ms, p99 300ms.
- Batch policy: adaptive batching with max batch size 16 and latency cap 150ms (we'll tune after first traces).
- KV/prefix caching: enable for repeated conversational contexts to improve p50 by ~20% in our tests.

Attachments and links I shared:
- redwood-verified-perf-profiles.pdf (short profiles for 7B/13B/30B variants)
- pilot prompt set: prompt-sets-lumera-v1.jsonl (example prompts we used for the benchmark)
- bench traces & raw traces link: https://s3.redwood.ai/buckets/lumera/pilot-traces/2026-03-15/

Open quality/regression concerns we flagged:
- Hallucination sensitivity on short Q&A when prompts are aggressively compressed — we recommend a human-eval prompt set to guard against regressions.
- Distribution shift: if your production inputs are longer than the samples used in our test, p95/p99 will shift non-linearly. We'll add a longer-input test in round 2.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Confirm SLA targets (throughput + latency + p99 tolerance).
2) We provision a two-week pilot environment (dedicated pool) and run the Redwood-provided benchmark (you'll get raw traces).
3) Post-benchmark, we meet to review perf dashboard and regression checks, then refine batch/cache policy.

Can you confirm the SLA targets and whether you want us to schedule provisioning for next Monday (03/22)?

Thanks — happy to adjust recommendations after you confirm.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

1) Cost sensitivity: for an initial 2-week pilot budget we want to keep avg spend under $6k — is Redwood-13B-int8 expected to stay within that for the throughput targets?
2) Latency: our users expect p50 < 150ms; p95 ideally < 350ms. We can accept a higher p99 for week 0 while we iterate.

If those targets are feasible, go ahead and provision for 03/22. Also: could you share estimated token cost per 1k output tokens for both candidate models?

Elise Turner

Looping in a few technical clarifications and a quick ops checklist from my side — Elise, replying inline to your asks.

Elise —
- Cost estimate: rough ballpark (cloud + infra + token usage) for a 2-week pilot at 15 rps sustained:
  - Redwood-13B-int8: ~$4.7k (server-side) + estimated token cost ~$0.8k = ~ $5.5k
  - Redwood-7B-quant (fallback-heavy scenario): ~$3.2k total
  These are conservative estimates; we'll provide a line-item breakdown once we provision.

- Latency feasibility: with the adaptive batching + KV caching settings Naomi suggested, your p50 and p95 targets are within reach on the 13B-int8 profile. The p99 depends on queue depth and tail network jitter; we'll instrument extra tracing to measure p99 and create a remediation plan (worker pool expansion + pre-warm).

Ops checklist for provisioning (what we need from Lumera):
1) VPN whitelist CIDR / VPC peering details (if provisioning in your VPC) or allowlist of IPs for hosted pilot.
2) Representative data samples (anonymized) for the longer-input test — drop in the S3 path above.
3) Acceptance criteria doc (simple pass/fail for perf + quality) — happy to draft if you want.

I attached a first-pass set of raw traces from the synthetic run we discussed (lumera-pilot-bench-traces.zip). Naomi — once Elise confirms, I'll schedule provisioning and enable the performance dashboard for Lumera.

—Jordan
